morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Compare the upper bracts and upper leaf surfaces. Snow-on-the-mountain usually has broader elliptic white-margined bracts, with the broadest point near the middle, and upper leaf surfaces that are mostly glabrous.
diagnostic_traits: largest bracts typically broad/elliptic rather than long-linear
capsule 3-lobed with relatively large rugose seeds

confusers.separator: E. marginata usually has broader elliptic bracts and mostly glabrous upper leaf surfaces; E. bicolor has long narrow bracts and conspicuous hairiness.

taxonomy.notes: POWO and Flora of North America both accept E. marginata and place Texas in the native range.

evidence_basis: Hays — Bill Carr's Coleman Ranch survey in Hays County lists Euphorbia marginata as native.
Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium specimen index documents Euphorbia marginata.
POWO and Flora of North America independently support Texas as native.
Kerr — Singhurst et al. 2010 vascular flora of Kerr Wildlife Management Area records Euphorbia marginata with voucher collections.

morphology.look_here_first: Broad white-margined distal leaves/bracts with mostly glabrous leaf surfaces, contrasted with the narrower, hairier E. bicolor.
morphology.key_separator: E. marginata has broader ovate/elliptic distal leaves and mostly glabrous surfaces; E. bicolor has much narrower white-margined bracts and conspicuous hairiness.
